extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and writers of prose fiction; readers interested in narrative technique and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical criteria for evaluating and producing prose fiction focused on narrative technique—how authorial voice, narration type, distance, reliability, realism, and 'showing vs telling' shape a reader's response and the work's moral and aesthetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the author's term for the means by which the writer makes known his vision to the reader and persuades him of its validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on the author's techniques for communicating vision and persuasion; the book argues rhetorical methods operate across ostensibly different stylistic schools (e.g., Fielding/Dickens vs. Flaubert/James/Joyce).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic purity and the rhetoric of fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic purity considered in relation to rhetorical choices in fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines tensions between ideals of 'pure' art and the rhetorical means authors use to shape reader response.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules I: 'True novels must be realistic'
rubrics_metrics.description: The maxim that true novels should be realistic as a guiding rule for fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers realism as a standard and how rhetorical technique supports or undermines claims to realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules II: 'All authors should be objective'
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule that authors ought to adopt an objective stance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigates objectivity as a normative expectation and its narrative implications for authorial presence and judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules III: 'True art ignores the audience'
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that authentic art disregards considerations of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzes the notion that the artist should not pander to audience expectation and how this affects rhetorical decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules IV: Emotions, beliefs, and the reader's objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: How emotions and beliefs interact with maintaining reader objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores the balance between eliciting emotion and preserving critical distance in readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of narration
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification and discussion of different narration modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the formal choices among narration types and their rhetorical effects on credibility, perspective, and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: The author's voice in fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the author's distinct voice and its role in fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on how authorial voice is manifested and controlled as a rhetorical instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: The uses of reliable commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: How reliable commentary functions within a fictional narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines when and why authors deploy reliable commentary and the effect on reader interpretation and moral judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling as showing: dramatized narrators, reliable and unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship between 'telling' and 'showing' via dramatized narrators and narrator reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers strategies where narrated summary ('telling') is dramatized and the implications of narrator reliability or unreliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of distance in Jane Austen's Emma
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of narrative distance control using Emma as a case study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates practical application of distance control techniques and their interpretive consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonal narration
rubrics_metrics.description: The mode and effects of impersonal (seemingly objective) narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigates the ideology and mechanics of impersonal narration and its claims to neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: The uses of authorial silence
rubrics_metrics.description: How withholding authorial comment (silence) is used rhetorically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers when silence functions as a persuasive or ethical strategy in shaping reader response.

rubrics_metrics.name: The price of impersonal narration I: Confusion of distance
rubrics_metrics.description: A critique of impersonal narration focusing on confusion created by uncertain narrative distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores risks where impersonal technique leads to ambiguous stance and reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: The price of impersonal narration II: Henry James and the unreliable narrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Further critique using Henry James to examine how impersonal narration can produce unreliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses James as an example of how claims to impersonality can mask or generate narrative unreliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: The morality of impersonal narration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical considerations surrounding the use of impersonal narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses moral implications of narrative stance and the responsibilities of the author toward readers and characters.
